1.title: Attacks and Their Impact
1.text: Welcome to Module eighteen: Attacks and Their Impact. It covers the exam area four point zero Network Security. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. four point two Summarize various types of attacks and their impact to the network: dos and D dos (distributed denial of service). V L A N hopping. M A C flooding. A R P poisoning and spoofing. D N S poisoning and spoofing. Rogue devices and services (D H C P, A P). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: four point zero Network Security (fourteen percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: Network attacks
1.text: Network attacks. The figure shows this: Common attacks mapped to the layer they target.

1.title: Network attacks, continued
1.text: Network attacks. dos or D dos. What happens: Floods a target so legitimate users cannot reach it; D dos uses many sources (botnet). Impact: Availability lost. V L A N hopping. What happens: Gets into another V L A N by switch spoofing (pretending to be a trunk) or double tagging. Impact: Segmentation bypassed. M A C flooding. What happens: Fills the switch's M A C table so it floods frames out every port. Impact: Eavesdropping, switch acts like a hub.

1.title: Network attacks, continued
1.text: Network attacks. A R P poisoning or spoofing. What happens: False A R P replies make hosts send traffic to the attacker's M A C. Impact: On-path interception on the L A N. D N S poisoning or spoofing. What happens: False D N S answers (or a poisoned cache) send users to the wrong I P address. Impact: Redirection to fake sites. Rogue D H C P server. What happens: Hands out wrong gateway or D N S settings. Impact: Traffic redirected. Rogue access point. What happens: An unauthorized A P connected to the network. Impact: A backdoor into the L A N.

1.title: Network attacks, continued
1.text: Network attacks. Evil twin. What happens: A fake A P copying a real S S I D. Impact: Credentials and traffic captured. On-path attack (formerly man-in-the-middle). What happens: The attacker sits between two parties and reads or changes traffic. Impact: Confidentiality and integrity lost. Exam tip: A switch flooding unknown frames out every port equals M A C flooding. Wrong gateway handed to clients equals rogue D H C P. A fake copy of the company Wi-Fi equals evil twin.

1.title: Social engineering and malware
1.text: Social engineering and malware. Phishing. Deceptive messages that trick users into revealing credentials or running malware. Dumpster diving. Searching trash for sensitive information (shred documents). Shoulder surfing. Watching someone enter a password or read a screen (privacy screens). Tailgating. Following an authorized person through a secured door (mantraps, badge checks). Malware. Malicious software: virus, worm, ransomware, trojan, spyware.

1.title: Impact
1.text: Impact. Attacks hit confidentiality (data exposed), integrity (data altered) or availability (service denied). Defenses are covered in Module nineteen (port security, D H C P snooping, dynamic A R P inspection, segmentation, training). Exam tip: Layer two attacks (M A C flooding, A R P poisoning, V L A N hopping) happen inside the L A N; port security and eight oh two dot one X defend against many. Exam tip: Attacks aimed at availability (dos, D dos) are different from attacks that intercept (A R P poisoning, evil twin, on-path). Name the goal first.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A switch begins forwarding traffic out all ports after its M A C address table is filled with bogus entries. What attack is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: M A C flooding. M A C flooding exhausts the C A M table.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Users receive the wrong default gateway from an unknown device on the L A N. What is the likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A rogue D H C P server. A rogue D H C P server hands out false settings.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Employees connect to a Wi-Fi network named like the company S S I D, and their credentials are captured. What is this attack? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: An evil twin. An evil twin copies a legitimate S S I D.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An attacker uses forged A R P replies to receive traffic meant for the default gateway. What type of attack results? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: An on-path attack. A R P poisoning places the attacker in the path.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An intruder follows an employee through a badge-controlled door. What is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Tailgating. Tailgating is following an authorized person into a secured area.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Thousands of compromised devices flood a web server with requests. What attack is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A distributed denial-of-service attack. Many sources attacking availability is D dos.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does M A C flooding target? Answer: The switch's M A C address table. Question two. How does V L A N hopping work? Answer: Through switch spoofing or double tagging. Question three. What is an on-path attack? Answer: An attacker positioned between two parties who reads or changes traffic.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is dumpster diving? Answer: Searching trash for sensitive information. Question five. What is shoulder surfing? Answer: Watching someone enter a password or read a screen. Question six. What does a rogue A P create? Answer: An unauthorized wireless backdoor into the network.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Layer two: M A C flooding, A R P poisoning, V L A N hopping, rogue D H C P. Wireless: evil twin, rogue A P. Name resolution: D N S poisoning and spoofing. Availability: dos, D dos. People: phishing, dumpster diving, shoulder surfing, tailgating. Position: on-path attack.
